subject: Processing geography and deletion roadmap — clarifications for evaluation

Subject: Processing geography & deletion clarifications for Redwood evaluation

Hi Priya / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Nutrivalue's security team is digging into where data will actually be processed and what deletion guarantees we can expect if we proceed. A few concrete Qs so we can move through procurement: 

1) Which cloud regions / countries perform inference for a standard hosted Redwood deployment for US customers?
2) Which subprocessors see customer content (prompts, model outputs, metadata)? Please list roles (e.g., model storage, telemetry, CDN).
3) Do you ever move data cross-border (esp. US <> EU) for hosted customers? If so, under what circumstances and what controls are in place (encryption, contractual safeguards)?
4) Retention & deletion: where are prompts, embeddings, and logs retained, by default, and what APIs or SLAs exist for deletion and audit evidence?

We're trying to confirm whether we need a Dedicated or Private deployment to avoid any cross-border movement of PII. Can you respond in a single Q&A email and share any supporting artifacts (subprocessor list / diagram)?

Appreciate it — if easier feel free to loop in legal.

Thanks,
Linda Cho
Head of Security, Nutrivalue Health

Hi Linda — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise Q&A and I attached our current subprocessor inventory and a region-routing diagram for reference. I also looped in Karthik (legal) for any contractual follow-ups.

Quick summary up front: for our hosted offering we process inference in the region you select (we default US customers to us-west-2 for primary processing, with us-east-1 as a failover/floor for capacity). We do not proactively copy customer content into unrelated geographic regions. Cross-border movement only happens under constrained conditions (controlled failover, customer opt-in to multi-region, or legal process). We offer Dedicated region-locked clusters and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) for customers that require no geographic export.

Q1 — Regions/countries:
- Hosted (default US): inference execution nodes run in AWS us-west-2 (primary). Failover capacity can run in us-east-1 (same country).
- EU customers: we run inference in eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 depending on region selection.
- APAC: ap-southeast-1 or ap-northeast-1 on request.
- Control plane (account/config metadata): hosted control plane is currently operated from the US; it holds minimal configuration metadata (no raw customer prompts), and we offer Private control plane options for EU-only control planes as part of Private deployments.

Q2 — Subprocessors and what they see (high level):
- Cloud providers (AWS/GCP): host inference nodes, ephemeral model artifacts; they may see encrypted model weights and transient memory (inference inputs/outputs) while processing.
- Persistent object storage (AWS S3 / GCS): used for model binaries, checkpoints, customer-managed artifacts. We encrypt everything at rest (AES-256).
- CDN / edge cache (Fastly / CloudFront): used for static assets and SDK artifacts; not for customer prompts by default.
- Observability / error reporting (Datadog / Sentry): receives telemetry and error traces; we scrub PII by default and only send hashed identifiers unless the customer enables detailed debug (opt-in).
- Secrets manager (HashiCorp Vault / AWS KMS): holds encryption keys; keys are customer-segregated for Dedicated/Private.
- Doc signing / procurement partners: see subprocessor inventory for contract details.

I've attached the subprocessor inventory file (subprocessor_inventory_aug2026.csv) which lists legal entity, location, role, and subprocessed data types.

Q3 — Cross-border movement:
- Default behavior: we keep inference execution and short-term caching within the customer-selected region for hosted customers.
- Exceptions that may cause cross-border movement:
  - Controlled failover when primary region is degraded — we fail over to a compatible region and record the event in audit logs.
  - Customer explicitly requests multi-region deployment or cross-region replication for latency/resilience.
  - Legal process (e.g., subpoena) where applicable and accompanied by legal safeguards.
- Controls: TLS 1.2+/mutual TLS for service-to-service traffic, at-rest encryption, contractual Standard Contractual Clauses where required, and data processing addenda (DPAs) that specify subprocessors and transfer mechanisms. For EU customers who require no export of customer content, we recommend Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) options.

Q4 — Retention & deletion:
- Inference inputs/outputs (prompts & generated tokens): default hosted retention = 30 days for troubleshooting and quality monitoring. This is configurable per-account and can be reduced to 0 days on request (or disabled entirely).
- KV / prefix caches: ephemeral by design — default retention is minutes to hours (workload dependent). They are not written to persistent logs unless a debug session is initiated (opt-in).
- Embeddings: not stored persistently by default unless you explicitly persist embeddings (customer-managed storage or opt-in feature).
- Logs & audit trails: infrastructure logs (access, errors) retained by default for 90 days; audit evidence for deletions is retained per your retention policy and can be exported on request.
- Deletion APIs & SLA: we provide deletion endpoints (DELETE /v1/objects, account-level purge) and can produce an audit package (timestamped deletion receipts) within 48 hours for standard ejections. For procurement-grade requests we can negotiate a shorter SLA in the contract.

Additional compliance notes:
- Encryption: TLS in transit; AES-256 at rest. Customer-managed keys supported in Dedicated/Private.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report (we will share under NDA), subprocessor attestation, and per-request deletion audit packages.

Attachments included:
- subprocessor_inventory_aug2026.csv (role, location, data types)
- redwood-region-routing-diagram.pdf (visual of routing & failover)

If you need a formal statement that no customer content will leave a specific country, we can prepare an addendum and propose Dedicated region-locking or a Private deployment. Karthik — can you flag any contractual language we should offer up front for Nutrivalue's procurement?

Next steps:
- Linda: tell us whether Nutrivalue requires a no-export guarantee for EU/US; if yes we will route this to Solutions + Legal to draft an addendum and propose Dedicated/Private options.
- If you'd like the SOC 2 and a short runbook on how deletion audit packages look, we can send both.

Best,

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed and the attachments look helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we move to procurement: 

- For Nutrivalue's use case we cannot have PII leave the US under any circumstance. Can you confirm that a hosted US region deployment with "no cross-border export" is contractually enforceable, or do we need Dedicated/Private to guarantee that?
- Please share a copy of the SOC 2 Type II report and the typical deletion audit package format (even redacted).

If you can confirm the above we can accelerate the PO. If Dedicated/Private is required, please include an order-of-magnitude estimate and timeline.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looping Legal (Karthik) helps.
